name: Optimize for endurance and resilience
definition: Navigate continuous pace and intensity, optimizing your own energy levels to sustain momentum for the long-term.

rows.under: Treats every week as a sprint with no recovery, or slows to a crawl and calls it balance.
rows.justRight: Navigates continuous pace without pretending it is a short burst. Plans the work so the team can keep going.
rows.over: Makes pace the only metric. Tired people are treated as a commitment problem.

rows.under: Avoids the hard stretch even when the work needs it. Intensity is never allowed.
rows.justRight: Can work at intensity when the outcome needs it, then return to a pace that lasts. Does not confuse a peak with the new normal.
rows.over: Stays at peak intensity after the need has passed. Intensity becomes the culture.

rows.under: Ignores their own limits until they fail. Energy is not part of the plan.
rows.justRight: Optimizes their own energy so they can sustain the work. Sleep, focus, and recovery are treated as part of delivery.
rows.over: Optimizes energy by handing every hard problem to someone else. Care for themselves becomes an excuse to step back from the outcome.

rows.under: Starts strong and fades. The work loses energy after the first push.
rows.justRight: Sustains momentum for the long term. The second month is as deliberate as the first week.
rows.over: Protects momentum by never stopping to think. The team cannot recover or redirect.

rows.under: Does not notice. Pushes the same plan onto people who are already spent.
rows.justRight: Notices when the team is spent and changes the load or the timeline so the work can continue. Endurance is a team problem, not a personal secret.
rows.over: Lowers the bar for the work in the name of resilience. Recovery becomes an absence of standards.
